title: The Alien Who Took Thor's Hammer
description: In Walt Simonson’s Thor #337–339, Beta Ray Bill wields Thor’s hammer, then faces Thor again without it. The duel shows why the alien warrior was worthy and leads to the forging of Stormbreaker.
hook: Thor's hammer gave his own opponent the power of thunder. The rematch showed why.
payoff: Thor got his hammer back, and Odin had a second one forged for Bill. Its name was Stormbreaker.

units.speaker: Host
units.text: Thor's hammer gave his own opponent the power of thunder. The rematch showed why.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: The alien was Beta Ray Bill. His people were fleeing danger, and when Thor approached their ship, Bill fought to protect them.
units.onscreen: BILL WAS GUARDING A REFUGEE FLEET
units.visual_query: BILL WAS GUARDING A REFUGEE FLEET

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: Bill got hold of Thor's hammer. It gave him Thor's power, and suddenly Odin had two worthy fighters and one hammer.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: Odin sent them to a world of fire. This time, they fought with their bare hands.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: Bill won. Then he saw Thor about to fall into the lava. He could have walked away.
units.onscreen: BILL WINS. THOR IS STILL IN DANGER.
units.visual_query: BILL WINS. THOR IS STILL IN DANGER.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: Instead, Bill grabbed him and pulled him to safety. He'd fought for the power to save his people, and he used his strength to save Thor too.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: Thor got his hammer back, and Odin had a second one forged for Bill. Its name was Stormbreaker.

units.speaker: Host
units.text: The hammer told us Bill was worthy. That hand reaching for Thor showed us why.
